commands.name: System load
commands.description:
Show uptime and load averages

Output includes current time, uptime, logged-in users, and 1/5/15-minute load averages

commands.name: Memory usage
commands.description:
Show memory and swap usage in human-readable units

Fields: total, used, free, shared, buff/cache, available

commands.name: Disk usage
commands.description:
Show disk space and filesystem types in human-readable form

Fields: Filesystem, Type, Size, Used, Avail, Use%, Mounted on

commands.name: Inode usage
commands.description:
Show inode usage per filesystem

When disk space remains but files cannot be created, check whether inodes are exhausted

commands.name: Kernel & arch
commands.description:
Show kernel version, hostname, and hardware architecture

Fields include kernel name, hostname, release, version, machine, processor, platform, OS

commands.name: Distro info
commands.description:
Show OS name and version

Common fields: NAME / PRETTY_NAME, VERSION_ID, ID (useful for package manager detection)

commands.name: CPU info
commands.description:
Show CPU architecture, cores, and frequency

Key fields: Architecture, CPU(s), threads/cores, Model name

commands.name: VM stats
commands.description:
Sample system stats 3 times at 1-second intervals

Fields: r/b run queue, si/so swap, us/sy/id/wa CPU shares

commands.name: Block devices
commands.description:
List disks, partitions, and mount points as a tree

Fields: NAME, FSTYPE, LABEL/UUID, MOUNTPOINT

commands.name: Logged-in users
commands.description:
Show logged-in users and their current commands

Also shows load and each session source/idle time

commands.name: Time & timezone
commands.description:
Show system time, timezone, and NTP sync status

Key fields: Local time, Time zone, NTP service, System clock synchronized

commands.name: Network connections
commands.description:
List TCP/UDP listening ports and processes

Flags: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -p process, -n numeric

commands.name: Socket stats
commands.description:
Modern netstat alternative for socket stats

Same common flags as netstat, usually faster

commands.name: Socket summary
commands.description:
Summarize TCP/UDP socket counts

Useful to spot TIME-WAIT / ESTAB buildup

commands.name: Interface addresses
commands.description:
Brief table of interfaces, state, and IP addresses

UP/DOWN state; address column includes IPv4 and IPv6

commands.name: Routing table
commands.description:
Show IPv4 routes

Default route usually starts with default via, then gateway and egress interface

commands.name: DNS config
commands.description:
Show DNS servers in use

nameserver lines are resolvers; search lines are default search domains

commands.name: Neighbor cache
commands.description:
Show ARP/NDP neighbor cache

Confirm LAN reachability and MAC addresses

commands.name: Ping test
commands.description:
Test network connectivity

-c 4: send 4 packets then stop; replace target as needed

commands.name: HTTP probe
commands.description:
Request headers only to check HTTP reachability

-I HEAD request; --max-time 10; replace URL as needed

commands.name: DNS lookup
commands.description:
Resolve a hostname via the system resolver

Uses local DNS config; closer to app resolution than a hard-coded public DNS

commands.name: Detailed listing
commands.description:
List directory contents in long format

-l long, -a hidden, -h human-readable sizes

commands.name: Find files
commands.description:
Recursively find files by name under the current directory

.: start dir; -name pattern; -type f files only

commands.name: Directory usage
commands.description:
Rank disk usage of immediate subdirectories

-x stay on filesystem; --max-depth=1; sort -hr; head top 20

commands.name: Find large files
commands.description:
Find files larger than 100MB on the current filesystem

-xdev no other mounts; -size +100M; first column is bytes

commands.name: Text search
commands.description:
Recursively search text under the current directory

-R recursive; -I skip binary; -n line numbers; replace pattern

commands.name: Recently modified
commands.description:
List files modified in the last 24 hours

-mtime -1; useful for recent logs/configs/temp files

commands.name: List archive
commands.description:
List tar.gz contents without extracting

-t list; -z gzip; -v details; replace archive name

commands.name: Process snapshot
commands.description:
Show detailed info for all processes

-a all terminals; -u user format; -x no controlling tty

commands.name: Process top
commands.description:
One-shot process status in batch mode then exit

-b batch; -n 1 once

commands.name: Top CPU
commands.description:
Top 15 processes by CPU usage

%CPU is a sample share; good for spotting CPU hogs

commands.name: Top memory
commands.description:
Top 15 processes by memory usage

%MEM is physical RAM share; RSS is resident memory

commands.name: Process tree
commands.description:
Show process parent/child tree

-a args; -p PIDs; output truncated to first 80 lines

commands.name: Find process by name
commands.description:
List matching PIDs and full command lines by name

-a cmdline; -f full match; replace sshd as needed

commands.name: Follow log
commands.description:
Follow a log file in real time

-f follow; replace path; some distros use /var/log/messages

commands.name: Log tail
commands.description:
Show last 100 log lines then exit

Useful without continuous follow; adjust path and count

commands.name: System journal
commands.description:
Recent system logs since this boot

-b this boot; -n 200; --no-pager

commands.name: Boot errors
commands.description:
Error-and-above journal entries since boot

-p err includes err/crit/alert/emerg

commands.name: Kernel log
commands.description:
Recent kernel ring buffer messages

-T human time; disks/NICs/OOM/driver errors are common

commands.name: SSH service log
commands.description:
Recent SSH service logs

Matches both ssh and sshd unit names across distros

commands.name: Running services
commands.description:
List currently running systemd services

Only state=running service units

commands.name: Failed units
commands.description:
List failed systemd units

Reports 0 loaded units listed when none failed

commands.name: Service status
commands.description:
Show status and recent logs for a service

-l no truncation; replace ssh with nginx/docker/etc.

commands.name: Enabled services
commands.description:
List services enabled at boot

enabled means start on boot; not the same as currently running

commands.name: Current user
commands.description:
Show current uid, gid, and groups

uid=0 is root; groups help check sudo/docker membership

commands.name: User list
commands.description:
List root and normal users, skipping most system accounts

Columns: username, uid, home, login shell

commands.name: Recent logins
commands.description:
Show 15 most recent logins

Includes user, source, login/logout; still logged in means active

commands.name: Failed logins
commands.description:
Show 15 most recent failed login attempts

Usually needs root; bursts may indicate password spraying

commands.name: sudo audit
commands.description:
Show recent sudo invocations

Audit who elevated privileges; some systems log to /var/log/auth.log
